findings.title: Why-dropped split vanishes for a class whose drops are exclusively 2.3 severed culls — 'every loss keeps a named cause' fails in the demolition corner
findings.location: app/main.odin:1476 (draw_sla_gauges guard) + app/main.odin:1366-1371 (feed growth) + core/flow.odin:856 (the silent cull)
findings.evidence: if acc.dropped > 0 && int(c) < len(app.drop_reasons) { — rows grow only from Drop_Site arrivals in feed_drop_sites; the 2.3 cull calls sla_count_drop with no site, so a severed-only class has no row and the whole split (incl. the 'severed N' residual the code promises) is hidden
findings.detail: The PR body claims the split 'always sums to the gauge's own drop N'. True once any E9/E22 site lands for the class; false for a class whose only losses are demolition strand-culls — exactly the scenario gap 4 exists to explain.
findings.recommended_fix: Drop the row-existence gate: when acc.dropped > 0 read app.drop_reasons[c] via a bounds-checked zero default (or pre-grow rows to len(cat.packet_types) at start_run) so 'severed N' always renders.

findings.title: The programmatic scratch pixel-scan (gauge fill / SHEDDING tag / marker anchors) is self-reported — no reproducible artifact in the repo
findings.location: PR body (Verification) + spec-v2-visibility.md:104-105 (the scratch is 'a separate throwaway' by design)
findings.evidence: PR body: 'Scratch pixel-scan (rlsw shadow + LoadImageFromScreen): pool bar fill, SHEDDING tag, and drop-marker positions verified programmatically' — no scratch script/output/image exists in the tree; LoadImageFromScreen appears only in harness/
findings.detail: T2-invisibility itself is PROVEN (capture path never calls draw_hud + Perkins' own 29/29 byte-identical harness re-run). What lacks durable evidence is the positive claim that the new surfaces render correctly. The 5.2 card set the same app-layer precedent, so this is a transparency gap, not a defect — but the claim cannot be re-verified from the repo.
findings.recommended_fix: Commit the scratch capture/scan script + output (or link where the evidence lives) so the verification is reproducible rather than self-reported; alternatively soften the PR-body claim to 'manually verified'.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS

findings.recommended_fix: Addressing W1/W2 (or accepting the app-layer no-durable-pixel-test precedent explicitly) raises the gate.

findings.title: draw_drop_markers doc says 'oldest mark anchors the fade'; the code aggregates and fades from the NEWEST shed
findings.evidence: doc: 'alpha fades over the window (oldest mark anchors the fade)' vs code: 'newest: u64' / 'if m.tick > agg[i].newest { agg[i].newest = m.tick }' / 'age := tick - bm.newest'
findings.detail: Comment-vs-code contradiction. The code's choice (re-shedding refreshes the marker) is arguably the right design; the doc line is stale. Demoted from the lens's warning: no behavioral defect.
findings.recommended_fix: Fix the doc comment to 'newest mark anchors the fade'.

findings.title: The QoS rejection toast draws over the new queue-depth row for its 30-tick life
findings.location: app/qos_panel.odin:475-476 (toast at panel bottom - 18) vs the queue-depth row (last row)
findings.evidence: draw_text(app, reject_label(app.last_reject), QOS_PANEL_X + 10, i32(panel.y + panel.height) - 18, 14, ...) — the depth row is the panel's last row
findings.detail: A rejected QoS edit hides the depth readout for ~1.5 s — exactly while the user is interacting with the panel. Transient and cosmetic.
findings.recommended_fix: Move the toast above the depth row (panel bottom - 18 - QOS_ROW_H) or draw the depth row above the toast anchor.

findings.title: Drop_Mark.class is written in feed_drop_sites but never read by either draw proc
findings.evidence: draw_drop_markers uses m.reason/m.bundle/m.lo/m.hi/m.tick; draw_pool_gauge uses m.reason/m.tick — m.class is never read
findings.detail: Dead field (presumably kept for future per-class marker coloring). Harmless; slight smell.
findings.recommended_fix: Either use it (per-class marker glyph/color) or drop it from the struct + feed.

findings.title: The card cause-line loop's 'int(c) >= len(cat.packet_types)' guard can never fire
findings.evidence: counts is sized make([dynamic]u32, len(cat.packet_types), ...) and the loop is 'for c in 0..<len(counts)' — c < len(counts) == len(cat.packet_types) always; node_stuck_by_class also guards p.class < len(counts)
findings.recommended_fix: Remove the guard or leave with a 'defensive' comment.

findings.title: 'Never overflows the 232 px frame' is not guaranteed — draw_text_c does not clip to width
findings.evidence: draw_text_c byte-copies and DrawTextEx's the full string — no width clipping; the cap-at-2-classes + '+N more' bounds the class COUNT, not the pixel width of long display names
findings.detail: Fits the shipped roster (Email/Streaming/...); a future long-named roster could overflow the card. Data-dependent, minor.
findings.recommended_fix: Truncate the cause line to a measured width, or leave documented as roster-bounded.

findings.title: node_stuck_by_class pin is single-scenario: mixed-class piles, counts-size guard, and the waiting_ticks==0 exclusion are never exercised
findings.evidence: one fixture (era 3, host) asserting total==2 && counts[1]==2 && counts[0]==0 + the dead-slot defensive case
findings.detail: The proc's other branches (class >= len(counts) guard, fresh-spawn exclusion, multi-class pile) are unpinned.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a mixed-class stuck scenario + a fresh-spawn (waiting_ticks==0) exclusion assertion.
